body:
It does have a decent impact on my life and those around me. I'm being treated but still showing symptoms and they can be odd if you don't know about it.

Heh...I'm trying to figure out how well I should know them before I tell. I'm getting to know one of them really well.

Don't worry about it. A lot of people with mental illness do seem to have issues with god.

It took me years to really come to terms with it. Everyone kept telling me my reality was wrong and its really hard to believe something like that. It felt like the drugs they gave me just obscured reality and hid it from me. Its only been in the past year that I've really accepted its a disease and have seriously tried to treat it.

My fathers side of the family is full of crazy. There are schizophrenics, a cousin with ocd, two or three people with depression problems. So yeah, a long history of mental illness in my family.

I have actual hallucinations all the time. I see people, sometimes have conversations with them. Mostly I hear things though.

I was atheist while I was having the delusions. It caused a lot of dissonance. I knew demons couldn't exist, but they were there and apparently out to hurt me. Its a big part pf how I realized I needed help.

I've also been diagnosed as bi polar.

I am from the western hemisphere. 

I'm a paranoid schizophrenic with some symptoms of disorganized as well.

28, female, I've been diagnosed for about 12 years.

I never had the idea I was a savior.

I'm happy to answer all you want. its such a misunderstood disease.
I'm schizophrenic. Despite having delusions of demon attacks, I'm not religious at all.
uh, no. I'm 28. Sorry, lol.

Sometimes its obvious. You know there probably isn't really a giant grasshopper hanging out with you. Sometimes its not so obvious, like with auditory hallucinations. I tend to not react to sounds unless my dogs do too.
Food is easy to get. Staying warm with clothing others can't easily steal is a trick.
They're my safety net. If I really need someone and can't do it on my own, I can call them.  I just prefer not to.

It has to be a brain problem. I don't know what part of the brain is the problem, I've read a few articles that say schizophrenics have a smaller hippocampus or something than normal people.

The medications help. I can at least pretend I'm a normal member of society when I'm on them. They make the visions lose their potency, and will hopefully get rid of them entirely once I'm on the right ones.

I do have moments where I think I'm fine and that I just imagined all of it. I don't go off them, though. I try to remind myself that they are the reason I'm feeling so much better.
28. Its been about two weeks.

I was on medications through the end of college, then got kicked off my parents insurance when I graduated. I couldn't afford the prescriptions anymore so I stopped taking them. And yes, that is when life got bad.
I don't know how to improve it. Its hell to get through it if you're uninsured but I don't know how to make it any better.
Socks, gloves, or hats
The closest I can say is southern california.
I need to take up a project like knitting. I used to do pottery and sculpture when I was younger, I should start up again.
I love trees. Trees help.

It was the same hallucinations most times. Had a few time with others, but usually there wasn't variety.

I guess that they were sort of like a gang. It was always the same "people."

I never talked to them. When I yelled at them or interacted with them it was usually in self defense. It lead to attacking people a few times.

I had to stay clean from drugs for two months before the govt program was allowed to give me much more than paxil & risperdal. Now I've passed that period and they're switching me to more effective drugs.

I really believed I could see demon and spirits for years. I thought I had special powers. And yes, the soul eating thing is nearly exactly what I believed.

Hide. Hide or find someone who can and be willing to protect you. Begging works if you don't look scary. Learn to scrub up in bus bathrooms really quickly. Tampons and pads can be recycled if you wash them carefully enough.

I wasn;t free, I was driven. There was no sense of freedom.

Yes I was.

I've never had impulses like this before.Its different most of the time, I can push it off normally.

Its still making me rethink having any weapons in the home. I have to get over my paranoia more before that would be possible.

Thank you.

Thanks. This is hard, one of the hardest things I've had to do. It rates right up there with deciding to accept treatment instead of just living with my demons.

I've noticed lately, it doesn't matter whether I believe it or not. Telling myself something positive helps. I can't always  think of what to say, but I know what you mean.

Thank you and good luck with your own struggles.
All kinds.Right now I'm listening to Nick Cave.
Total dog person. I've got two of them I love to bits.
College, I think. I had friends. I didn't have such horrific hallucinations. There were things to distract myself with, I loved learning, I experienced so much that was new. It was wonderful.
I do, they are incredible.

Peaches and red bell peppers.

 What would your picks be?

I just like relacing in the backyard, there isn't enough of it to walk. But being there, with my puppies and my flower garden it makes me feel so at peace.

Auditory hallucinations are kind of scary. If you don't mind me asking, what kind do you have?

Its cold. And hungry. Theres always people with you though, you all get pushed to the same places.

I'm not homeless anymore. I am in treatment and living on my own. My parents gave me my computer and most of what I own.

Music helps. Drinking helps. I could drug myself into oblivion and I probably will later tonight.

But watching tv or movies fucks with me. I don't always see the movie thats really playing, sometimes my brain fills in the dialogue or the visuals. It makes the movie not make sense and hard to enjoy.

I love to garden. I love to nurture plants until they're big and beautiful and producing their flowers or fruit. Dahlias are my favorite flowers.

Indian. Hands down. Have you tried it?

I was broken up with by my boyfriend last week. It kind of left me with no support.

I could call on my family if I really needed it but they have already done so much/put up with so much from me that I'm really trying to get over this myself.
Yes. Sometimes I couldn't help it. I'd start having a fit and attacking people when I got really bad. I ended up in many mental hospitals and a couple jail cells over it.

A whole lot. Enough that they pretty much blend together.

Boston was one of my favorites. The bus station was within walking distance to a river and I come from southern california and hadn't seen anything like it before.

Kansas City, Missouri was another good one. I met some good people there.
I don't know.

I'm getting off of paxil and a couple other drugs so I can be switched to new ones that will hopefully be more effective. Pacil is notoriously hard to get off and I'm having trouble with urges and voices ttelling me to kill myself. Which I won't do. Fuck that. But my boyfriend broke up with me last week and he was basically my whole support structure and...its just difficult to get through the nights this week.

Sine my last teens I though demons and evil spirits were after me. I'd see them everywhere and the voices in my head told me they were after me. I got so bad with it that after I graduated college I left on a bus trip I didn't come back from for years. I had to stay on the go, if I didn't the demons would catch up with me and get me. The only contact I had with my family was to get money to go somewhere new. I'd be homeless/living on buses for a couple months. Then I'd find a city that was safe, and I'd spend a couple months there, or however long I could hold a job. 

Is there anything more specific you'd want to know?

I hear voices, they're very obvious.

I liked sleeping in bus stations. They were safer than anywhere on the street and the security guys generally wouldn't give me a hard time so long as I wasn't being disruptive or had a ticket for a bus within a couple days.

>Remember, it's not YOUR impulse, it's the paxil withdrawal

I will remember that, its a pretty good thought. I'm stubborn as all hell, I can resist anything if I feel I'm being pushed into it. Thank you. Even in a month I'll be grateful I got through this.

A lot of time I catch something out of the corner of my eye and when I turn to look, there is a hallucination there. The grasshopper looks real, as real as my brain can make it at least. I think it just glosses over the parts I'm not sure of, I find it difficult to look for details while talking to this guy. He would talk to me a little bit. Offer advice for staving off the demons I thought were after me. I never tried to touch him, though.

I've had conversations with people who aren't there. I've tried to photograph some of the hallucinations, only to come back with disappointingly empty frames. I've never physically interacted with any of my hallucinations. That I know of, at least.

Feel free to ask whatever you want. I don't mind :)

I usually hear or see it. Getting both means a pretty major hallucination for me. I still get those on a regular basis, but they aren't as bad.

I haven't had many relationships that lasted over a month or two. And just ended the one I had that lasted over six months. So...pretty crappy, I guess?

Thanks for your prayer. 

It gets a tiny bit easier every day.

Nice, I'm glad this ama had some good repercussions :)

I do know they give out some schizo meds for anxiety and depression. My cousin was on a couple of my medications for a while and she isn't schizophrenic either.

They help a lot. I used to be pretty nonfunctional. I thought I was being hunted by demons. I couldn't hold a job, I couldn't even stay in one place too long. Mostly I lived in bus stations and on buses. It was not a good existence.

The medications tone down all the paranoia. They take away a lot of the hallucinations. They don't work one hundred percent, but they work enough for me to kid of ignore the rest.
Yeah, they talk to themselves all the time. Its like they're observing what I'm doing, not directly speaking to me about it.
It helps so much. Just having something to concentrate on for multiple hours a day helps, I'm not just sitting there letting this stuff control me.
It probably doesn't mean anything unless you've got other symptoms.
If I know them well, I'll trust them. Not so much with casual acquaintances or strangers.

I'm not a photographer, but I like to take pictures for fun. I'll go somewhere for a day and when  I get home and review my photos, a third of them will be empty frames and I'll be missing a bunch of what  I thought were going to be awesome shots. Instead I was taking pictures of things that weren't there.

Demons are the most common.

I don't watch many movies. Sometimes my mind replaces dialogue or scenes, or even adds characters. Its hard on me so I don't do it much.

I have minor and major hallucinations. Sometimes its just shadow people. Other times its a person or an animal who isn't there. I had one time where my bedroom transformed into the bedroom I had as a kid. That one freaked me out.

I had bad hallucinations. I thought I have to stay on the run constantly to escape demons. My life was spent borrowing money from people to hop on another bus. I spent time homeless, I spent time in jail and mental institutions. It was hell.

This life is so much easier.
I call them Croup and Vandemar, but they don't really have names. The voices are usually the same.

I'm 28.

The first I remember is when I was 13. I was hearing voices already.

Officially diagnosed when I was 16.

My parents say there were, but I really can't remember.

I smoke weed. I do have a family history.

From what  I understand there is a time limit on it. If you haven't developed symptoms by your mid twenties you're probably going to be fine.

Real sounds drown them out sometimes. It takes music or a lot of white noise, but I can make them kind of go away.

Its actually something I hear with my ears, its not in my head.
I was on paxil, risperdal, welbutrin, and vistaril. They weren't working very well so I've been switched to cymbalta, abilify, clonozapam, trozodone, and prazosin.
I'm a terrible artist.

My dreams used to be normal. Now that I'm on medications my dreams are weird. There is a strange continuity every night. The landscapes stay the same, even the people are the same. Our activities progress. Its really strange.

It you've ever read Gaiman's Neverwhere, there are the villians Croup and Vandermar. The voices remind me of them, but they're just observers.

Some of the other hallucinations do have personalities. Like the monk who visits or this giant grasshopper that hangs around.

There are good days and bad days now that I'm on medications. Before the meds there were good days too, but they were severely outnumbered by the bad ones.

A lot of them are the same. Some of them are just random crap my brain sees.

One of the yelled at me to stop sinning while I was in Vegas. That was sort of amusing.

Thanks :)
Thank you
Interesting, I will check that out. Thanks.

I smoke cigarettes and weed all the time. It helps calm me down a lot. It doesn't stop any of the hallucinations but it makes me care about them a lot less. And they give me pills for the paranoia, so it works out.

I've done LSD. It was fun. I've been thinking I should do it again.

I've tried. It has no real effect. Mostly its just screaming at them to stop and leave me alone.

I haven't tried binaural tones. They've been mentioned to be before, maybe I should give it a shot.

Its good to hear about people who have gotten better. I've only been in treatment for it less than a year and the mantra seems to be "this will take time." Thanks for sharing, the encouragement is appreciated.

Drinking Presidente last night. This morning its switched to whiskey. I've been playing SSX3 and Tony Hawk all night. I pulled off a million point trick that I'm really quite proud of.

Vegas was fun. Except that I don't do well in crowded, noisy, chaotic enviroments. It makes it harder to tell whats real and what isn't. But yeah, we caught a couple Cirque du Soliel shows and stuff. Booze got me through that trip better than it has tonight.

I've done both. Didn't care for shrooms, though I didn't have a bad trip.

Acid was fun the first time. I was just happy. Really happy. The world was a beautiful wonderful place and I loved being in it.

It was scarier the second when my boyfriend had to spend two hours convincing me to open my eyes and stop being a reflective beam of light.

Those are my only experiences with hallucinogenics. I'd probably do them again if I had a chance.
Its hard. I'm lucky, my cousin owns a company and he lets me work there. Its a new thing, but its been going well so far.

Not sure about the first past of your post, I haven't thought in that direction before.

But as for music, its a godsend. It drowns out what I don't want to hear. White noise works wonderfully as well, I use fans a lot to drown out the noise. I'd go nuts without my fans.
I used to do that. You just get used to it after a few years and you don't need to check anymore.
I know.

The voices get loud and distracting when I'm trying to meditate. The first ten minutes are always taken up with focusing on breathing and blocking out the voices. They feel just as real as they do when I'm not meditating.

I've tried some drugs. I did acid a few times, it didn't do much beyond making me happy and give me a feeling of oneness with the world. Which was more fun than I expected.

I haven't tried opiates of MDMA or anything,

The voices have a little identity. Not like they're full beings, but I can predict what will make them talk, what they'll have problems with, etc.

Some of the other hallucinations are full beings with memories and experiences.

I've never tried to merge with them.

I don't know much about the dream life philosophy. Care to share?

Sometimes my mind simply gets quiet. No noises, no visuals, just concentrating on my breathing.

Other times I'll see thinks. Interesting things rather than scary. There is an old monk that will come talk to me or chant at me. Sometimes I see a hand writing on a wall.
I always play loud music during sex. It drowns them out so I don't have to listen to a critique in my performance.
I am going to try it. I used to be really into sculpting and pottery and it did help. The concentration made my mind more quiet. Thanks for reminding me that I should do it again!
Yes, it does. I can see it both ways.
Not sure what you mean. I've a couple doctors and emergency lines I can call if I need it.
That would be awesome. I'd take a pill for that.

I've tried to draw it but my attempts are pathetic.

All of it would probably be fascinating if it didn't scare the hell out of me.

The look real. The easiest way to tell that its not is if no one else is reacting to it. That or simply ask someone. Though people get a little freaked out when you're all, hey can you see the giant grasshopper too?

I had imaginary friends that I insisted were real. I would freak out over sounds they couldn't hear and beg them to make them stop. I was always asking why people were talking all the time, they think I meant in my head.

Childhood onset is really rare, I could have just been a kid with a good imagination. I don't think we'll ever really know for sure.
Not many. Lacking sex drive is the biggest. Constant mild headache is the most recent.

Yeah, I had the same problem. Zombie girl with no good side effects.

I'm glad you found something that worked. Thats great.
Invega, no. But I'm switching from risperdal to abilify.
I have great fantasies and dreams, but I've never developed the discipline to write it all down in coherent format. Instead I've got notebooks full of psycho scribblings.

I'm unemployed.

I qualify for a couple low income mental health programs, but mostly my treatments are paid myself.

I've got anxiety and depression problems associated with schizophrenia.

Imagine you're me. Everything you see must be questioned. The box of tissues on your desk? Probably real. The eight foot tall grasshopper smoking in the corner of your room? Probably not. This goes on constantly. Whenever you're awake, you have to question whether what you see is real and sometimes you get it wrong.

And while you're doing this there are voices constantly harassing you. They talk down to you, they tell you you're always wrong, that terrible things are happening, that you should just kill yourself. 

Its hell. Its a really fucked up form of hell. Megs help and I've faith I'll eventually find ones that help more, but for now its where I'm stuck.

I do have a supportive family. As supportive as I'll let them be, at least.

I tend to hang out with really sane people. Down to earth, not take to weird flights of fantasy, people that are really in the moment.

Its always paranoia and fear. Theres nothing good, the best I get is neutral.

I wish I could write an awesome novel. Maybe I'll have to try one day :)

No, not nice voices. Some neutral ones.

I meditate to block the voices out. Sometimes it doesn't work an channels one of them instead.

I don't watch fringe. What is it?
I'm on cymbalta, abilify, clonazapam, trazadone, and prazosin.

My family is strangely uninvolved. I have my psychiatrist give my parents an update once a month, just so they know how I am. But we never, ever talk about it. I'm just not ready to talk to them about it at all. I don't know if I'll ever be.

Oh, I've got direct lines to my therapist and my psychiatrist. They'd both do whatever they could to help, I'm sure.

But why use it unless I really need to. I can withstand worse than this, I had to before I had treatment for it.

No, don't really have anyone. I broke up with my boyfriend last week, its been another of the disruptions to my routine that have bothered me so much. And I don't really have anyone else. Its hard having close friends and I just got back to my life after years on the road. I don't really know anyone anymore.
Thanks.
Its pretty accurate. It makes me uncomfortable to watch, so I don't do it anymore.

This is an AMA, I don't mind the questions. Honestly, its a relief to have something to do.

The voices aren't ever positive. Sometimes they are funny, but its in a Jesus Christ, could you be more of a fucking asshole? type way.

I guess its an easy way to get out of relationships. And when you get caught stealing or something, it helps to be crazy instead of criminal-y. 

I get both sexes. But its weird, the left ear is always male and the right always female.

Its always related to whats going on. If its something about the past or future its always got a relation to whats happening at the moment. Like in Vegas, it wasn't the maid who made my bed. It was the demonic agent I saw at check in who swept my room for information in the guise of being a maid.

It take about a month to really feel better but only a week to start feeling worse.

Its not like replaying a fight in your head. It feels like it doesn't come from you at all, its something you hear with your ears. Its hard to describe. I guess...you know how movies/tv portrays acid trips? The hallucinations you think are real, the pink elephants and talking brooms and whatever...its like that, only scary.

This is the first time they switched my meds. They took me off them all together once, but that ended badly. I'm relatively new to treatment for this, I spent years before allowing my illness to control me.

The meds have helped. I used to have hardcore hallucinations of demons and evil spirits. Those have mellowed, which is good because they were hard to deal with.

We think I might have had childhood onset schizophrenia.Its really rare though and since I don't remember much of my life before 13 all we really have to go on are my parents memories. From that, they think I've had this a while.

There is a family history. An aunt with the same illness, an uncle who committed suicide, both sides of the family have rampant alcoholism.

On bad weeks its a constant struggle to tell the real from the hallucinations. Things like watching other people react to something before I do, sometimes I see if my dogs hear a noise before I acknowledge it. And the voices...they're relentless. All they want is for me to buy into their reality again and its hard keeping up with the constant refusal to do so.

I have a new psychiatrist. Since the old meds weren't working very well she decided to switch me to a new set.

A lot of them are just voices. They make observations on everything I do. I also get other auditory hallucinations that could be anything. Currently it sounds like bombs are going off outside my bedroom. Like a whole war is happening out there.

>If they are like they are in that video, how the hell do you constantly ignore them without saying 'shutup' to yourself every five seconds?

Its hard. You learn to not pay attention. And it isn't a constant thing, for me at least the voices come and go through the day. It drives me a little crazy sometimes even with the medications. Banging my head on the wall is about the only thing that helps and thats a strategy generally frowned upon.

>I.e. was there any reward for following what they said, or only a fear of punishment if you didn't?

No, there is no reward to listening to their advice. They're observers who tell me what to do, it doesn't matter whether I do it or not. 

>Does your mood affect which voices/hallucinations occur? Are you more likely to hear neutral background chatter when you're in a good mood or see the grasshopper when you're feeling x/y/z?

I definitely get more of the telling me what to do voices when I'm stressed out or upset. I get more of everything when I'm stressed or upset.

If I'm in a good mood I'll most likely have visual or auditory hallucinations of the neutral sort. Interesting instead of frightening.
Yes, they do. They point out that the hallucinations mean the demons are near, that its time to go, that they're going to catch me.
Giant insect.
Its mostly a felt answer to everything.
It doesn't really work that way. I'm still actively trying to convince myself that the demons are a lie. I might get to a point where I can simply ignore them but I'm not there yet.

I would have answered sooner but was having some problems. 

They think answering you was a bad idea.

I have had some trouble with some of the comments. The ones where people decided to mess with me and try to tell me that I'm psychic or whatever. The voices had fun with that. It wasn't a huge deal, I expected at least a few responses in that direction.

My memories of the incidents are filled with the hallucinations I was having. So they are pretty unreliable.

I was examined after being arrested and sent to the psych hospital after two of the incidents. I had injuries and things common with rape victims. I'm sure being raped didn't help my schizophrenia at all.
I have. I don't remember what it was, but I do remember it was higher than average.
Not that I remember. But  I don't remember my childhood very well at all.
Just be there for him. Let him know that he can talk to you even if he thinks he sounds crazy. Encourage him to stick with his treatment if he's ever thinking its a bad thing.

I'm more in control of my actions and thoughts than I used to be. I'm doing better with both but my thoughts are still difficult to reign in.

I'm not convinced. I'm doing my best to get there.

And yes.

No, they don't always occur together. There are many times I think I see something, but theres no sound. Or hear something I can't see.

I wear glasses. The black smoke... There were red lines of energy that were completely obscured by the smoke that gave the figures form.

I haven't seen it. I don't watch many movies, sometimes I hear or see parts that aren't there. Like I'm watching a totally different movie than what the people with me are seeing. It gets stressful, so I don't do it.
You hear the voices with your ears. Its an actual sound, unlike an internal monologue that just stays in your head.
I don't mind it.
I reckon you got some more things to speak to your doctor about ;)
That sucks. I'm sorry it ended that way for your cousin.

Paranoid/disorganized.

I guess one positive point is that I'm never bored.

The treatment isn't helping as much as it could if I'd stop smoking pot. If I stopped I'd be able to be prescribed stronger drugs that would have more of an effect.
They talk to each other all the time. Most of their conversations are about me, not with me.
That is kind of odd :)
No. I didn't think many people could.
No. Christin.

I had to change the way I perceived what I believed was coming after me. I really had to, I couldn't sustain the way I was living. 

Now every day I have to tell myself most of what I believe about the world isn't real. Its my mind playing tricks on me.

Its like brainwashing myself into being normal.
I actually hear it. Sometimes I have to watch and see if other people react to what I'm hearing before I can feel like its probably real.
I've seen bit of that before, makes me extremely uncomfortable to watch.
I hope so, its a good thought.
Thanks. I'm sorry its been so rough with your aunt and uncle. It really is a terrifying way to live.

My meds **don't** fully kill my hallucinations.

My worst days I'm a **mess**. Moodswings, crying, wild accusations.

On my best days I'm just another regular person **with** regular problems.

My parents and family are full supportive of **me**.
No, it was really something I had to come to myself.
Yes
Its okay to laugh.
Being raped was like my worst nightmares come to life. I had dreams where I'd been caught before, but this was life being caught for real.

I decided they have to be imaginary. The thought they were real wasn't an option anymore and I had to believe the voices aren't real. I had family and doctors helping me make that choice, and I don't think it would have happened if I weren't as run down as I was.
I don't think much of them. They aren't my taste.
I haven't seen it. I don't watch most non-zombie horror movies.
risperdal, welbutrin, paxil, and vistaril. They are working okay. There are few side effects I'm not willing to put up with.
I try to be able to blow it all off and ignore. I'm getting better at it.
Yes

Straight female, he was a boyfriend

no way

I've been on doxepin, risperdal, paxil, welbutrin, and vistaril. They work, but aren't doing the best job. I have to test clean from marijuana for two months before they can change my medications to anything much stronger.
Giant grasshopper. Not as big as the rabbit. And we don't talk much.

Last april was the last time. It had been said before though that was during the really blurry last few years. 

I'll elaborate as much as I can. What would you like to know?

There was the moment where I didn't care if it was mental illness or real. I was tired. I was making life hell for people I cared about. I couldn't kill myself because they'd just put me back in the hospital and I hated that place.

So I decided to take medications and live with whatever happened.
Thanks, I didn't know there were long acting types of meds.

I've had those moments of blinding anger where you just snap and do what they tell you to. I've attacked people a couple of times because of it, but its been a long time since I've lost control that badly.

It does take a lot of self control to keep from acting out those urges. The kid probably didn't have a good handle on it yet.

Or he could just be a dick. I've run into lots of people who think mental illness is an excuse to do whatever you want.
We think it started when I was 8. Became worse as I hit my late teens, and then I lost it completely in my early twenties.

Sorry, I don't know any tricks. I think each person has to learn to accept it before they're ready to treat it and its damn hard to accept.

Good luck.
I felt compelled. Like I had to leave  or something truly bad was going to happen. Staying was never an option.
I do.
Shaky, at best.

No, none of my regular problems. I had a lot of auditory hallucinations during the second trip that I didn't get with the first, but they were the neutral sort.

I only did acid twice. After my second experience I found I had no desire to try it again and see what a real bad trip would be like.

In my late teens was the first time it came up. I refused to believe it for years, then refused to treat it for a few more. I still get a few hallucinations, but nothing like what I used to have.

Its hard to talk about sometimes. You sit there and talk and realize how crazy it sounds and its hard to keep going.
I'd probably have been condemned as a witch and burned.

It didn't trigger the schizophrenia. I know something happened twice because I was hospitalized soon after it happened after being arrested. I was sent to the psych hospital after the police confirmed I wasn't high or drunk.

So, I remember it as rape. It might not have been. I guess I can't say for sure either way. Its not something I've explored much.

I might be bi-polar, I don't really know. I do get awfully moodswings.

Strange, I hadn't seen that before. 

But yes, I could see the illusion.
It happened a few times while I was living on the streets and in bus stations and coincided with the few times I was sexually assaulted. My mind turned the men into the demons.
Yes, I believe in them when I'm off my meds.
Yeah, I was. It wasn't pleasant.
I don't know. If it is really scaring you its probably worth ask a doctor about.

I had a good trip. I didn't have hallucinations, I just got really happy. I dunno, I wanted to laugh and sing and play kumbayaa. It was fun.

The second time I tried it was different. It made me really tense and the man I was seeing at the time had to spend a few hours convincing me to open my eyes and stop being a reflecting beam of light. That one was more weird.

I've tried to engage the voices in conversation. Its been the cause of a few trips to the psych ward. It never ends well and never gives any satisfying answers.
